subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which term best describes a person who takes the risk of setting up and running a business?
options: Entrepreneur
Shareholder
Stakeholder
Employee
questions.explain: An entrepreneur is the individual who takes the financial risk of starting and running a business venture.

questions.q: Adding value means a business does which of the following?
options: Makes the selling price higher than the cost of the inputs
Reduces the wages it pays its workers
Increases the number of employees it hires
Lowers its selling price below its costs
questions.explain: Adding value is the difference between the price charged and the cost of the bought-in materials and inputs.

questions.q: Why might a strong brand image help a business to add value to its products?
options: It allows the business to charge a higher price than rivals
It removes all of the business's fixed costs
It guarantees the business will never make a loss
It means the business no longer needs to advertise
questions.explain: A recognised, trusted brand lets customers accept a premium price, increasing the value added per unit.

questions.q: Which of these is a key characteristic commonly associated with a successful entrepreneur?
options: Willingness to take calculated risks
A refusal to make any decisions
An unwillingness to work long hours
A preference for avoiding all responsibility
questions.explain: Entrepreneurs must be prepared to take considered risks in pursuit of a business opportunity.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a business plan?
options: To set out the aims of the business and how they will be achieved
To calculate the exact profit the business will earn
To replace the need for any market research
To guarantee a bank loan is approved
questions.explain: A business plan documents the business's objectives and the strategy, finance and resources needed to reach them.

questions.q: A sole trader is best described as a business that is:
options: Owned and controlled by one person
Owned by shareholders who buy shares
Run jointly by between two and twenty partners
Owned by the government
questions.explain: A sole trader is a business owned and controlled by a single individual.

questions.q: What does limited liability mean for the owners of a private limited company?
options: They can only lose the money they have invested in the business
They are personally responsible for all business debts
They cannot sell any of their shares
They pay no tax on business profits
questions.explain: Limited liability protects owners' personal assets; their loss is limited to the amount they invested.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of forming a private limited company (Ltd) rather than remaining a sole trader?
options: The owners gain the protection of limited liability
The business no longer needs to keep any accounts
Profits are automatically higher every year
The owners avoid all legal formalities
questions.explain: Incorporating as an Ltd gives shareholders limited liability, protecting their personal assets.

questions.q: Priya runs a market stall as a sole trader. The business fails owing £15,000. What is the consequence of her unlimited liability?
options: She may have to sell personal possessions to pay the £15,000 debt
Her losses are limited to the money she put into the stall
The debt is written off because she is a sole trader
Only the business's assets can be used to repay the debt
questions.explain: With unlimited liability there is no legal separation, so a sole trader's personal assets can be claimed to settle business debts.

questions.q: In the term 'SMART objectives', what does the 'M' stand for?
options: Measurable
Motivating
Marketable
Maximised
questions.explain: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Realistic and Time-bound.

questions.q: Which of the following is most likely to be the main aim of a new business in its first year of trading?
options: Survival
Rapid international expansion
Maximising dividends for shareholders
Dominating the global market
questions.explain: New businesses commonly prioritise survival while they establish themselves and build a customer base.

questions.q: What is the difference between a business aim and a business objective?
options: An aim is a general long-term goal, while an objective is a specific target to help achieve it
An aim is short-term, while an objective is always long-term
An aim must be financial, while an objective must be social
There is no difference; the terms mean exactly the same
questions.explain: Aims are broad overall goals, whereas objectives are the specific, often SMART, targets set to achieve those aims.

questions.q: A cafe sets the target: 'Increase sales revenue by 10% within the next 12 months.' Which SMART element is shown by the phrase 'within the next 12 months'?
options: Time-bound
Measurable
Achievable
Specific
questions.explain: Setting a clear deadline of 12 months makes the objective time-bound.

questions.q: The marketing mix is traditionally made up of which four elements?
options: Product, Price, Place and Promotion
People, Profit, Place and Product
Price, Profit, Promotion and People
Product, Profit, Place and Promotion
questions.explain: The marketing mix is commonly known as the 4Ps: Product, Price, Place and Promotion.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of primary market research?
options: Carrying out a customer survey
Reading a government population report
Using data from a competitor's website
Looking at a published market research report
questions.explain: Primary research gathers new, first-hand data directly, for example through surveys, questionnaires or interviews.

questions.q: Why do businesses divide a market into segments?
options: To target products more closely at groups of customers with similar needs
To remove the need to carry out any market research
To guarantee that every customer buys the product
To avoid having to set a price for the product
questions.explain: Segmentation groups customers by shared characteristics so marketing can be targeted more effectively.

questions.q: Which statement best describes quantitative market research data?
options: It is numerical data that can be measured and analysed statistically
It is opinion-based data about why customers feel a certain way
It can only be gathered from secondary sources
It cannot be shown in charts or graphs
questions.explain: Quantitative data is numerical and measurable, unlike qualitative data which explores opinions and reasons.

questions.q: A business wants to quickly and cheaply find out the size of a market before launching. Which research method is most appropriate?
options: Secondary research using existing published reports
Commissioning a large new nationwide survey
Running long face-to-face interviews with every customer
Building a new product and test-marketing it nationally
questions.explain: Secondary research reuses existing data, making it faster and cheaper than gathering new primary data.

questions.q: Which document lists the duties and responsibilities of a particular job?
options: Job description
Person specification
Job advertisement
Contract of employment
questions.explain: A job description sets out the tasks, duties and responsibilities involved in a specific role.

questions.q: What is an advantage to a business of recruiting internally rather than externally?
options: The candidate is already known and cheaper to recruit
It always brings completely new ideas into the business
It increases the total number of employees in the business
It avoids the need for any interviews at all
questions.explain: Internal recruitment is usually quicker and cheaper, and the candidate's abilities are already known to the employer.
